m.s: Pat the rind of {pork_roast} bone dry with paper towel. If you can, leave it uncovered in the fridge overnight so it dries out. Score the rind in lines 1cm apart with a sharp knife, cutting into the fat but not the meat. Rub with oil and plenty of salt, getting it into the cuts.
Heat the oven to 240°C. Roast the pork on a rack in a roasting tin for 30 minutes until the rind bubbles and blisters. Turn the oven down to 170°C and roast for 2 hours more.
Cut {potato}, {swpotato} and {carrot} into chunks, toss with oil and salt on a tray and roast below the pork for the last hour, turning halfway, until golden.

If the crackling isn't crunchy all over, put the pork under a hot grill for 3 to 5 minutes and watch it closely, as it goes from perfect to burnt fast. Rest the pork for 15 minutes, uncovered so the crackling stays crisp.

Pour the pan juices into a small saucepan and skim off most of the fat. Add {stockpowder} dissolved in 1 cup hot water and bring to a simmer. Mix {cornflour} with a splash of cold water, whisk it in and simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy.
Finely shred the cabbage and cut {apple} into matchsticks. Toss with {mayo}, a squeeze of lemon if you have one and a pinch of salt. Carve the pork and serve with the veg, gravy and slaw.

l: Pork and veg together, gravy in a little container. Pork and slaw rolls work well too. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
g: Use 100% maize cornflour (not "wheaten") and check the stock powder. Everything else is naturally GF.
